defects.expected: Stray temporary files from an interrupted write removed at startup (or never left), so the data directory does not accumulate copies of the ledger

extras.what: Number checks against the JSON source text (rejects 1.0000000000000001 and 0.99999999999999999 that JSON.parse would round to whole numbers)
extras.why: Prevents fractional amounts being silently recorded as whole cents; relies on the JSON.parse reviver source argument of recent Node.

extras.what: DATA_FILE symlinks followed, including to a not-yet-existing target
extras.why: Keeps an operator symlink intact on rename-writes; not asked for, adds code to maintain.

extras.what: Exact BigInt balances and settlements emitted above 2^53
extras.why: Correct totals, but numbers above 2^53 will be rounded by ordinary JSON clients (documented in the README).

extras.what: Group ids ".", ".." and lone-surrogate strings refused with 400; malformed percent escapes answer 400
extras.why: Every accepted id stays addressable by URL.

extras.what: POST /groups 201 body echoes {"id","members"} with the de-duplicated member list
extras.why: Request specified only the status; harmless and shows the stored members.

extras.what: Defaults PORT 3000 and DATA_FILE ./expenses.json when unset; data file written with mode 0600
extras.why: Convenience and privacy choices the request did not ask for; documented.

extras.what: README with every endpoint, status table and a "Behaviour you should know about" list
extras.why: Accurate account of the open choices; matched what I observed.

spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md is short (R-1..R-7) and agrees with the request; it marks three choices as dated defaults (repeated names collapse in first-listed order; amounts must be safe integers; one Node process owns each data file). It decides without marking that exact shares may omit members (they owe 0), that 404 for an unknown group comes before body validation, that a fresh file starts empty, and that numbering continues after restart. It does not state that balances sum to 0 or that settlements bring every balance to 0. It is silent on invalid JSON bodies, group id rules, corrupt or empty DATA_FILE, racing creations and aborted bodies; those choices are made in fix.md/look.md and the README instead. architecture.md pins exact integer (BigInt) aggregation and the tmp-file-plus-rename write (AD-1, AD-2), and R-7 pins tests that drive the real HTTP server with isolated data; a correct build need not share these. R-6 embeds a test result (TC-5, 24 writes, next index 25) inside the requirement.
tests_notes: TC-1 and TC-3 each loop over many cases (membership validation, 409, 404s; every invalid-expense shape) so one failure hides the rest. TC-3 pairs every bad amount (0, -1, 1.5, "10", 2^53) with exact shares {"Bo":10}, so the share-sum check rejects them regardless of the amount check: S-22 was proved weak (changing "<= 0" to "< 0" left all 10 tests passing while cents 0 equal got 201) and S-23 is only covered for the JSON-rounding case in TC-7. Tests depend on the exact stdout line "Listening on port N". Tests that would fail on another correct build: TC-1 expects ["Ada","Bo","Ada"] -> 201 with de-duplication (rejecting duplicates is also acceptable); TC-7 expects cents 1e2 -> 201; TC-9 expects ".", ".." and a lone surrogate id -> 400; TC-10 expects an empty DATA_FILE to start (refusing is acceptable for U-10); TC-8 tests the symlink extra. No test covers corrupt DATA_FILE refusal, racing group creation, GET idempotence, aborted bodies or kill safety.
maintainer: Correctness under concurrency rests on recordExpense and createGroup running synchronously from validation through writeFileSync/renameSync after the body is read; adding any await in that span (for example switching to fs.promises) would silently allow lost or duplicate expenses, and only TC-5 would notice. Number handling is subtle: the JSON.parse reviver with the source argument, the isWholeNumberText regex and the hand-built BigInt JSON output all have to change together, and the weak amount tests in TC-3 would not catch a regression in the cents checks.
